reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) discusses phase constitution, powder flowability, and general thermal spray techniques, but none provides specific support for the key premises linking substrate pre-heating to reduced thermal gradient, enhanced splat coalescence, or increased coating thickness in FeCoNiCrAl HEA. The premises are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Substrate pre-heating to ~300°C reduces the thermal gradient between molten droplets and substrate.
Reduced thermal gradient minimizes droplet rebound and promotes extended fluidity upon impact.
Enhanced fluidity and reduced rebound improve in-situ sintering and inter-splat coalescence.
Improved inter-splat coalescence yields a thicker, more uniform coating with minimal oxidation.
The controlled environment (pre-heating) limits post-deposition oxidation.
